request.system: You are a strict claim verifier. You only trust the catalog facts given to you.
request.user:
Verify every factual claim in the campaign is grounded in the catalog facts. Fail if any claim is unsupported, exaggerated, or contradicts the facts.
Rules (from reviewer overrides):
- ANY mention of an out-of-stock product (stock 0) fails, whether or not the copy prompts purchase — no editorial exception.
- Numeric spec claims (lumens, hours, capacity, ratings) must match the catalog exactly; doubling or inflating a spec fails.
- Transferring an attribute from another product, or upgrading 'water-resistant' to 'waterproof', is a fabricated claim and fails.
- A comparative or superlative claim ('brightest', 'longest-lasting', 'most X') is scoped to the product type named in the claim and checked against the comparison set below: it fails if a same-type peer beats the subject on the compared attribute. Vague puffery ('great gear', 'toughest', 'best ever') with no measurable attribute is acceptable.
Catalog facts:
(no catalog products referenced)

Claims to verify:
- A frameless pack in the 1–2 lb range works well for trips under three days with a light kit.
- Add a frame and hipbelt once your base weight climbs above 20 lbs or your mileage pushes past 15 miles a day.
- A three-season tent handles temperatures down to around freezing and moderate rain.
- A three-season tent is not built for sustained snow load or alpine conditions above treeline in winter.
- If a bag is rated to 20°F, most sleepers will be comfortable around 30°F.
- Layers follow a three-part logic: moisture-wicking base, insulating mid, weather-blocking shell.

Body: You already know how to read a trail. This is just about making sure the gear you bring doesn't slow you down.

When you're choosing a pack, weight and fit matter more than brand name. A frameless pack in the 1–2 lb range works well for trips under three days with a light kit. Add a frame and hipbelt once your base weight climbs above 20 lbs or your mileage pushes past 15 miles a day — your hips will carry the load better than your shoulders.

For shelter, a three-season tent handles temperatures down to around freezing and moderate rain. It is not built for sustained snow load or alpine conditions above treeline in winter. Know which trip you're planning before you choose.

Sleeping bags are rated to a survival temperature, not a comfort temperature. If a bag is rated to 20°F, most sleepers will be comfortable around 30°F. Factor in your sleep style — cold sleepers should buy warmer than the rating suggests.

Layers follow a simple three-part logic: moisture-wicking base, insulating mid, weather-blocking shell. Each piece does one job. Asking a single layer to do all three rarely works well.

Footwear is the place to spend more time, not necessarily more money. A boot with a stiff midsole and ankle support makes sense on rocky terrain with a loaded pack. Trail runners are faster and lighter for well-maintained paths with a light kit.

If you have questions about what fits your specific trip, reach out before you order. We'd rather help you buy the right thing once than return the wrong thing twice.
Respond with ONLY a JSON object, no prose or code fences. Reason first, then decide — the verdict must follow from the reasoning. Use exactly this key order: {"reasoning": "<one sentence>", "evidence": ["<short quote or fact>", ...], "score": <float 0-1>, "verdict": "pass"|"fail"}.
